Subject. Extract from North China Daily News entitled "No Crime to be
a Communist"

Made by. D. S. I. Logan Forwarded by. D. I. Crawford

The attached extract from the April 16th
issue of the North China Daily News, entitled
"No Crime To Be A Communist" was taken to the
M. A.'s Office on 17.4.40, with a view to
ascertaining whether the S.S.D.Court had received
any instructions on the law relating to Communists.

The matter was taken up with the President
of the Court by Mr. Lee, A/M.A. and the following
information conveyed to the Special Branch by
Inspector Pike, attached to the M.A.'s Office,
on 25.4.40, viz :-

"The only thing a supposed Communist can
be charged with is Endangering the Internal
Security of the Chinese Republic."

（左侧方框内文字）
Commr. of Police.

事由。摘自《字林西报》题为“成为共产党人并非犯罪”的摘录

制作人。D. S. I. Logan 转呈人。D. I. Crawford

附件为1940年4月16日《字林西报》中题为“成为共产党人并非犯罪”的摘录，该摘录已于1940年4月17日送至市公署律师办公室，旨在查明上海特区地方法院是否已收到有关共产党相关法律的指示。

此事由市公署代理律师 Lee 先生向法院院长提出，随后由市公署律师办公室附属警员 Pike 于1940年4月25日向特别股传达如下信息，即：

“所谓共产党人唯一可被指控的罪名是危害中华民国内部安全。”

Chinese Regulations

A Chinese Communist charged in
a Shanghai court with endangering
the Republic of China may be
declared not guilty because the
Regulations Governing the Punish-
ment of Those Endangering the
Existence of the Republic have
been revised. This has just been
revealed in the Third Branch
Kiangsu High Court where Judge
Wu acquitted Hsiung Yu-wu, an
alleged member of the Chinese
Communist Party, who has been
wanted by the French police here
for some years and who is still at
large.

The judgment simply reads that
Hsiung Yu-wu, who is charged with
endangering the Republic, is ac-
quitted. It was also said in Court
that although the police have been
looking for Hsiung for six years,
they have not been able to find him.
He was summoned by the Court
several times but he failed to appear
and the Court had then to serve
public notice, but he again did not
make an appearance.

The Supreme Court studied the
case and referred it to the High
Court where a lawyer was appointed
to present arguments in favour of
defendant. The case was discussed in
Court and the Judge stated that
since the regulations had been
revised there could be no punish-
ment for Hsiung. In the past he
might have been sentenced to heavy
prison terms or death.

Hsiung was wanted together with
several other Communists including
Mrs. Ho Lung, wife of the famous
Chinese Red army leader who is
now fighting on the front, and Ho
Kan-chung, brother of the general.
Mrs. Ho and the general's brother
were arrested six years ago. The
former has already served her
prison term, while the latter died
of illness during imprisonment.

成为共产党人
并非犯罪

被通缉六年之人
根据中国最新法规
被判无罪

一名在上海法院被控危害中华民国的中国共产党员，可能因《危害民国紧急治罪法》的修订而被宣告无罪。这一情况刚刚在江苏高等法院第三分院披露，该院法官吴氏宣判熊雨吾（Hsiung Yu-wu，音译）无罪，熊系 alleged 中国共产党成员，已被上海法国警察通缉数年，目前仍在逃。

判决书仅写明，被控危害民国的熊雨吾被判无罪。法庭上还提到，尽管警方搜寻熊某已达六年，但一直未能将其抓获。法院曾多次传唤他，但他未出庭，法院随后不得不发布公告，但他再次未露面。

最高法院研究了此案，并将其发回高等法院，高等法院指定了一名律师代表被告进行辩护。案件在法庭上进行了讨论，法官表示，由于法规已修订，无法对熊某进行处罚。在过去，他可能会被判处长期监禁或死刑。

熊某与包括贺龙夫人（Mrs. Ho Lung，音译）在内的其他几名共产党人一同被通缉，贺龙是著名的中国红军领袖，目前正在前线作战；还有贺龙的兄弟贺干忠（Ho Kan-chung，音译）。贺夫人和将军的兄弟于六年前被捕。前者已服完刑期，而后者在监禁期间因病去世。

Party during the present Sino-Japanese conflict.

Made by D.I. Kuh Pao Hwa Forwards. by C. Crawford D. I.

In order to promote cooperation between the Kuomintang
and the Chinese Communist Party, and to improve the direction
of military operations during the present resistance-campaign
against Japanese aggression, the National Government has
recently invited Messrs Chow Ung Lai (周恩來), Secretary
of the Chinese Communist Party, Mao Shih Tung (毛澤東),
a red army commander, and Zing Paung Shien (秦邦憲), alias
Boh Koo (博古), a standing committee member of the Com-
munist Central, to be advisors of the State Council, while
the Chinese Communist Party has, at the same time, establish-
ed a Liaison Office in Hankow with Gen. Yih Kien Ying (葉劍英),
prominent figure in the Canton Uprising in 1927, and Mr. Pan
Han Nien (潘漢年), a member of the Propaganda Department of
the Chinese Communist Party, in charge.

Apart from making the above arrangements, the National
Government has re-adjusted the various fronts as follows:-

Area Responsible Defensive Forces and Commanders
Shansi, Shensi and The 8th Route Army (former red
Charhar Provinces. troops) under Generals Chu Teh
(朱德) and Peng Teh Hwei
(彭德懷).
Honan Province. Central troops under Gen. Liu
Chih (劉峙).
Shantung Province. Provincial troops under Gen.
Han Fu Chu (韓復榘).
Northern Kiangsu with Central and Kwangsi troops under
Hsuchow as Headquarters the command of Gen. Li Chung Jen
at present. (李宗仁), the prominent Kwangsi
military commander.

为促进国民党与中国共产党的合作，并改善当前抗日军事行动的指导，国民政府最近邀请中国共产党秘书长周恩来 (Chow Ung Lai)、红军指挥官毛泽东 (Mao Shih Tung) 以及中共中央常务委员秦邦宪 (Zing Paung Shien)，别名博古 (Boh Koo)，担任行政院顾问；同时，中国共产党在汉口设立了联络处，由1927年广州起义中的重要人物叶剑英将军 (Yih Kien Ying) 和中国共产党宣传部成员潘汉年先生 (Pan Han Nien) 负责。

IMPORTANT CHANGES
ARE FORESHADOWED

Former Red Leaders In
China Are Invited To
Important Posts

Since the fall of Nanking important changes in the military, political, and economic situation of the country are to be noticed. All efforts are being made to mobilize the entire country, to carry on armed resistance to the bitter end, states the "Social Daily News."

Military Affairs: General Chiang Kai-shek, Chairman of the Military Affairs Commission, will make changes and readjustments in the command on various fronts. The Shansi-Shensi front, it is reported, will be delegated to the Eighth Route Army, all troops being placed under the command of Generals Chu Teh, Peng Teh-hwai, Hsu Hsiang-chen, and other ex-Red Army commanders, who will be appointed to various important military posts in Shansi and Shensi provinces.

On the Peiping-Hankow Railway, General Li Tsung-jen will be appointed commander of the Chinese forces, being shifted from his present station on the Tientsin-Pukow line. The troops on the Tientsin-Pukow Railway will be placed under the command of General Tang Sheng-chih. On the Kiangsi and Anhwei fronts, the troops stationed there from Yunnan, Kweichow, Szechwan, and Hunan will be put under the command of General Pai Tsung-hai. On the Chekiang and Fukien front, the crack units of Generals Hsieh Yu, Miao Pei-nan, Wu Chi-wei and Hwang Chi-hsiang are stationed, with General Cheng Fa-kwei as commander-in-chief in this area. In South China, if serious fighting expands to that area, General Li Chi-sen will be appointed commander-in-chief at Canton.

Political Affairs
Important changes will be made in the government at Chungking. Mr. Chou En-li and General Mao Tse-tung, leaders of the former Chinese Soviet districts, will be appointed to high positions in the government. General Mao and Mr. Chou, who have been stationed at Yenan and Linfeng respectively, have arrived at Nanchang in response to a summons from General Chiang Kai-shek. Both of them will play an important political role in the future. The State Council, the highest Government organ, will have from five to seven members.

前红军领导人

《社会日报》称，自南京陷落以来，国家的军事、政治和经济局势发生了重大变化。各方正全力动员全国，将武装抵抗进行到底。

军事事务：军事委员会委员长蒋介石将军将对各战区的指挥进行调整和重新部署。据报道，晋陕战区将交由第八路军负责，所有部队均由朱德、彭德怀、徐向前 (Hsu Hsiang-chen，音译) 及其他前红军指挥官指挥，他们将被任命为山西和陕西省的各种重要军事职务。

在平汉铁路沿线，李宗仁 (Li Tsung-jen) 将军将被任命为中国军队指挥官，他从目前所在的津浦线调任。津浦铁路沿线的部队将由唐生智 (Tang Sheng-chih，音译) 将军指挥。在江西和安徽前线，驻扎在那里的云南、贵州、四川和湖南部队将由白崇禧 (Pai Tsung-hai) 将军指挥。在浙江和福建前线，部署着谢裕 (Hsieh Yu，音译)、缪培南 (Miao Pei-nan，音译)、吴奇伟 (Wu Chi-wei，音译) 和黄琪翔 (Hwang Chi-hsiang，音译) 等将军的精锐部队，该地区的总司令为张发奎 (Cheng Fa-kwei，音译) 将军。在华南地区，如果战事严重扩大至该区域，李济深 (Li Chi-sen) 将军将被任命为广州总司令。

政治事务
重庆政府将进行重大改组。前中国苏维埃地区领导人周恩来先生和毛泽东将军将在政府中担任高职。毛将军和周先生分别驻守延安和林丰 (Linfeng，音译)，应蒋介石将军的召唤已抵达南昌。两人未来将在政治上发挥重要作用。行政院作为最高政府机构，将有五至七名成员。

Kuomintang-Red
Unity Arranged

Communists Ask United
Front Against Japan
In Xmas Message

(United Press)
HANKOW, Dec. 28.—Indication
that plans were afoot for per-
manent and intimate co-operation
between the Chinese Communist
Party and the Kuomintang in
forming a united front against
Japanese aggression was given in
a manifesto issued Christmas Day
by the Communist Party.

The manifesto, issued in con-
nection with the current situa-
tion, declared interalia, "The
Central Headquarters of the
Chinese Communist Party wishes
to announce to the entire nation
that there is a strengthening of
intimate co-operation between
the Kuomintang and the Com-
munist Party in the great his-
torical task to consolidate a na-
tional united front against Ja-
panese aggression."

Hope Realized.

"The two parties have now
not only realized the absolute
necessity to co-operate but they
have become determined to effect
a more intimate union.

The Chinese Communist Party
has decided to co-operate with
the Kuomintang not only during
the campaign of resistance against
the Japanese but also after the
eventual victory, in the work to
construct a new China.

"At the present dangerous
juncture, the Communist Party
likes to suggest that the Chinese
nation should perform along the
following lines:

"1. Mobilize all national mili-
tary material and financial re-
sources and man power. Do our
utmost to resist aggression
against us and in North China
and regain lost territory.

"2. Consolidate, enlarge and
unify the national Revolutionary
Armies.

Stronger Government

"3. Strengthen the National
Government.

"4. Carry out the National
Defense Council's policies.

"5. Organize the masses to
take part in the anti-Japanese
struggle and strengthen the
national defense.

"6. Implement immediately
the program of political reform
so as to arouse the enthusiasm
of the people and strengthen
national unity.

Diplomatic Busy
(United Press)
HANKOW, Dec 28.—Coincident-
al with the United States having
expressed satisfaction with the
settlement of the Peasay incident,
observers here were noting with
interest today maneuvers on the
Sino-Soviet diplomatic front.

They attached more than a
passing significance to the appoint-
ment of the new Russian Am-
bassador to China, the sudden
arrival of Mr. Wang Min, Com-
missar delegate after a five-year
stay in Moscow, and the impend-
ing return of the Chinese Am-
bassador from Moscow. Interest
was also centered on unofficial
reports of the appointment of Mr.
Tso Tsung Fan as the new Ambassador to
Russia.

Mr. Tso Tsung Fan this morning
left for Japan in an official
capacity. He will be succeeded
by Mr. Sun Fo who has been
appointed Ambassador to Russia.

（批：s/o ok 29/2）
（批：D.J. Ld C 30/12 of 1/v）

29376

国共合作已达成安排

共产党在圣诞文告中呼吁建立抗日统一战线

（合众社）
汉口，12月28日电。——中国共产党于圣诞节发表的一份宣言表明，中共与国民党正着手计划进行永久且密切的合作，以组成抗日统一战线。

该宣言结合当前局势发布，其中宣称：“中国共产党中央委员会愿向全国宣告，在巩固抗日民族统一战线这一伟大历史任务中，国民党与共产党之间的密切合作正在加强。”

希望实现。

“两党不仅已认识到合作的绝对必要性，而且已决心实现更紧密的联合。

中国共产党决定不仅在抗战期间与国民党合作，而且在最终胜利后，在建设新中国的工作中也将与国民党合作。

“在此危险关头，共产党建议中华民族应按以下方针行事：

“1. 动员全国一切军事物资、财政资源和人力。竭尽全力抵抗对我国及华北的侵略，并收复失地。

2. 巩固、扩大并统一国民革命军。

更强有力的政府

“3. 加强国民政府。

4. 执行国防委员会的政策。

5. 组织民众参加抗日斗争，加强国防。

6. 立即实施政治改革方案，以激发人民热情，加强民族团结。

外交活动频繁
（合众社）
汉口，12月28日电。——随着美国表示对皮斯利（Peasay）事件的解决感到满意，这里的观察家今天饶有兴致地注意到中苏外交战线上的动向。

他们赋予新任俄国驻华大使的任命、在华沙（原文如此，疑为莫斯科）停留五年后突然抵达的委员代表王明先生，以及中国驻莫斯科大使即将回国等事件以非同寻常的意义。人们的兴趣还集中在关于左宗藩（Tso Tsung Fan，音译）被任命为新任驻俄大使的非官方报道上。

左宗藩先生今天上午以官方身份启程前往日本。他将由已被任命为驻俄大使的孙科（Sun Fo，即孙佛/孙科，音译）接替。

Russian Help
Said Welcome

Red Manifesto Banned;
USSR Said Only One
To Extend Aid

(Transocean-Kuo Min)
HANKOW, Dec. 28.—A Trans-
ocean representative today inter-
viewed a number of leading Chi-
nese personalities in order to dis-
cover their views concerning the
rumors that China was on the
way to being "Bolshevized."
At the headquarters of the Chi-
nese Communist party he receiv-
ed the assurance that although
the party still continued to exist
it had nevertheless renounced for
the time being the carrying out
of its program of confiscation of
private property and the over-
throw of the existing govern-
ment of China.
Cooperation
The danger to which China was
exposed had caused the Com-
munist party to seek cooperation
with the Central Government in
order to strengthen the resistance
to Japan. Therefore the Red
Army as such had been dissolved
and its men incorporated in
the Central army.
It was further stated that the
Communist party did not insist
on Soviet Russia's intervention
but would welcome help from any
side. The policy of the Chinese
Communist party after the war
would not be foreseen. It was
impossible to say what shape
it would take. At present as a local
party it would be prepared to work
together with the government in
full consciousness of its respon-
sibilities as a responsible party.
Appeal To Nation
The Communist spokesman
thereupon transmitted the latest
party manifesto which will be
published shortly. The manifesto
appeals to the Chinese nation to
make the necessary sacrifices in
order to strengthen national resis-
tance and to create united China.
Inquiries at the offices of the
leading Chinese newspapers have
revealed the fact that by order of
the government the manifesto had
not been admitted for publication
as the Kuomintang was cautious
to prevent any intensified Com-
munist propaganda.
The official spokesman of the
Communist party stated that the
influence of the Communist party
was increasing. He added that in
China there existed a Com-
munist party but this only
existed in order to carry
out certain tasks in connection
with the struggle against Japan.
Friendly Gesture
In reply to the question whe-
ther the forthcoming reconstitu-
tion of the Chinese government
might result in placing certain
Communist leaders in leading
positions as a friendly gesture
towards Moscow, the Foreign
Office spokesman declared that
this was not intended.
The spokesman admitted that
China maintained friendly rela-
tions with Moscow. In the belief
that help might be more easily
obtained from Soviet Russia, who
had already given proof of her
goodwill by sending arms, aer-
oplanes and other war material.
The Soviet Union had also sent
advisers to China. This was done
in order to facilitate the delivery
of war material.

据称欢迎俄国援助

红色宣言被禁；据称苏联是唯一提供援助者

（跨洋通讯社-国民通讯社）
汉口，12月28日电。——一名跨洋通讯社代表今日采访了一些中国知名人士，以了解他们对有关中国正走向“布尔什维克化”谣言的看法。
在中国共产党总部，他得到保证，虽然该党仍然存在，但目前已暂时放弃执行没收私有财产和推翻中国现有政府的纲领。
合作
中国所面临的危险促使共产党寻求与中央政府合作，以加强对日抵抗。因此，红军作为一个实体已被解散，其人员编入中央军队。
此外还声明，共产党并不坚持要求苏俄干预，但欢迎来自任何方面的帮助。战后中国共产党的政策尚不可预见。无法说清它将采取何种形式。目前，作为一个地方性政党，它准备在充分意识到其作为负责任政党的责任的情况下，与政府合作。
呼吁全国
共产党发言人随后转交了最新的党派宣言，该宣言不久将公布。宣言呼吁中华民族做出必要的牺牲，以加强民族抵抗并创建一个统一的中国。
在对主要中文报社的查询中发现，根据政府命令，该宣言未被允许刊登，因为国民党谨慎地防止任何加剧的共产主义宣传。
共产党官方发言人表示，共产党的影响力正在增加。他补充说，中国存在一个共产党，但其存在仅仅是为了执行与抗日斗争有关的某些任务。
友好姿态
在回答即将重组的中国政府是否可能作为一种对莫斯科的友好姿态，将某些共产党领导人安置在领导职位上的问题时，外交部发言人声明这并非本意。
发言人承认中国与莫斯科保持着友好关系。人们相信，从已经通过运送武器、飞机和其他战争物资证明其善意的苏俄那里，可能更容易获得帮助。苏联还向中国派遣了顾问。此举旨在促进战争物资的交付。

December 30, 1937.                                Afternoon Translation.

To Lei Wen Pao of Dec.29 and other local newspapers (Hankow
telegram):

CHINESE COMMUNIST PARTY ISSUES MANIFESTO

The following manifesto was issued by the
Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party on
Christmas Day:-
"The co-operation between the Communist Party
and the Kuomintang to strengthen the united front against
Japan is being gradually intensified.    The Communist
Party and the Kuomintang have decided to establish closer
relationship in future.    Besides co-operating with
the Kuomintang during the period of military operations
against Japan, the Chinese Communist Party will work
with the Kuomintang for the reconstruction of a modern
China after final victory has been achieved.    At this
time of national crisis, the following work should be
carried out immediately:-
1) A mobilisation of the human power, materials and
financial resources of the country.    Every effort be
made to prolong the resistance in North China and to
defend Hankow.
2) The revolutionary troops throughout the country be
strengthened and enlarged.
3) The organization of the National Government be
strengthened.
4) An economic policy for the defence of the nation be
enforced.
5) The people of the country be organized to participate
in anti-Japanese hostilities.
6) The propaganda work be expanded.
"We are confident that China will defeat the
Japanese Imperialists, because the democratic nations
throughout the world are in sympathy with China.    The
people of Japan and of the world detest the Japanese
militarists."

S!
)

D. J. Reid

中国共产党发表宣言

中国共产党中央委员会于圣诞节发表了如下宣言：
“共产党与国民党加强抗日统一战线的合作正在逐步加强。    共产党与国民党已决定在未来建立更密切的关系。    除了在针对日本的军事行动期间与国民党合作外，中国共产党将在取得最终胜利后，与国民党共同致力于现代中国的重建。    在这个国家危机时刻，应立即开展以下工作：
1) 动员全国的人力、物资和财政资源。    尽一切努力延长在华北的抵抗并保卫汉口。
2) 加强和扩大全国的革命部队。
3) 加强国民政府的组织。
4) 实施保卫国家的经济政策。
5) 组织全国人民参加抗日敌对行动。
6) 扩大宣传工作。
“我们确信中国将击败日本帝国主义者，因为全世界的民主国家都同情中国。    日本人民和世界人民都憎恨日本军国主义者。”

Subject Brief resume of the political situation in China in 1937:
Reconciliation between the Kuomintang and the Chinese Communist Party.
Made by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.S.

In October 1936 - prior to the Sian Coup d'Etat - the
Chinese Communist Party changed its original policy of "class
struggle" and endeavoured to adopt a programme of co-operation
with the Kuomintang with a view to achieving a common front
against the incessant Japanese aggression. In the early stages,
the Nanking Government doubted the sincerity of the communists,
but, as the necessity for future co-operation between the two
parties became increasingly apparent, negotiations through an
exchange of representatives appointed by Nanking to Nga-Yao-pao
(瓦窑堡), then the Red capital in North Shensi, or vice versa,
were carried out. Nothing tangible, however, resulted from
these conversations, and when the Sian incident of November
12, 1936 occurred, all hope of liaison between the two parties
was abandoned. However, strange to say, the incident accelerated
the delayed union - the formation of a united front against
national aggression, especially Japan.

During the Sian Coup d'Etat (November 12 to December 25)
certain leaders of the Chinese Communist Party, such as Mao
Shih-tung (毛泽东), commander of the Red Army, Chow En-lai
(周恩来), once Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party, and
Zing Paung-shien (秦邦宪), ex-Chief of the Chinese Communist
Youth League, were given an opportunity of conferring with
Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek, when an amicable understanding
was reached. This conference gave rise to many false rumours
which were calculated to camouflage the real motives for
convening the conference. The conclusion of an agreement
containing eight clauses was, however, emphatically denied by
both parties.

On his return to the South, Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek

主题 1937年中国政治局势简要综述：
国民党与中国共产党的和解。
由督察顾保华（Kuh Pao-hwa，音译）撰写，由克劳福德（C. Crawford）副督察转发。

1936年10月——在西安事变之前——中国共产党改变了其原有的“阶级斗争”政策，并试图采取与国民党合作的方案，以期实现共同阵线，对抗日本不断的侵略。在初期，南京政府对共产党的诚意表示怀疑，但是，随着两党未来合作的必要性日益明显，双方通过交换代表进行了谈判，南京指派代表前往当时位于陕西北部的红色首都瓦窑堡（Nga-Yao-pao），反之亦然。然而，这些会谈并未产生任何实质性的结果，而当1936年11月12日西安事变发生时，两党之间联络的所有希望都被放弃了。然而，奇怪的是，该事件加速了迟来的联合——即形成反对民族侵略，特别是反对日本的统一战线。

在西安事变期间（11月12日至12月25日），中国共产党的一些领导人，如红军指挥官毛泽东（Mao Shih-tung）、前中国共产党书记周恩来（Chow En-lai）和前中国共产主义青年团负责人秦邦宪（Zing Paung-shien，音译），获得了与蒋介石总司令会谈的机会，并达成了友好的谅解。这次会议引发了许多旨在掩盖召开会议真实动机的虚假谣言。然而，双方坚决否认达成了一项包含八项条款的协议。

蒋介石总司令返回南方后

Date July 2. 1937.
Subject Alleged visit of Mr. Chow Ung Lai, Vice-Chairman of the Revolutionary Military Council of the Chinese Communist Party, in Shanghai and the present relations between the Kuomintang and the Communist Party.
Made by Clerk Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by I. Boyne O.S.I

With reference to the attached newspaper reports to the effect that Mr. Chow Ung Lai, Vice-Chairman of the Revolutionary Military Council of the Chinese Communist Party, recently visited Shanghai with the object of re-organizing the Party, I have to state that this information lacks confirmation. The report probably arises out of the following circumstances:-

Following the conclusion of a rapprochement during the Spring of 1937 in consequence of the Sian incident between the Communist Party and the Nanking Government, the former issued an order instructing that the "Central Political Bureau" (中央政治局) (chief executive organ) together with its various branches be replaced by organs to be entitled "District Offices of the Special Area of the Chinese Republic."

In May 1937 one named Chang Kuo Zou (張國燾), a member of the Communist Party, was appointed by the Party to take charge of the "Shanghai Office of the Special Area of the Chinese Republic" (中華民國特區駐沪辦事處). At the beginning of June Chang was instructed to invite local professors to proceed to the North West to give lectures to students of the North West University in Shensi. At the same time he was given, through another member of the Communist Party, several letters written by Mr. Chow Ung Lai and addressed to some of the professors who were formerly friends of Mr. Chow. On being approached by Chang with these letters the professors suspected that Mr. Chow was in Shanghai hence the outcome of the rumour of Mr. Chow's visit here.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No.......... 7794
S.1, Special Branch
REPORT
Date....... June 23, 1937.

Subject Alleged visit of Chinese Communist leader in Shanghai.

Made by D.S. Kamashita Forwarded by [Signature]

With reference to the attached translations from the
"Diamond", a Chinese newspaper in its issue of June 18, and the
Nippo, a Japanese newspaper in its issue of June 22, 1937,
regarding the visit to Shanghai of Chow Ung Lai (周恩来), a
Chinese communist leader: I have to state that the origin of
the information is unknown. However, the information is
reported by the Japanese paper mentioned above to have emanated
from Chinese quarters. Judging from the fact that the
information regarding Chow Ung Lai's visit to Shanghai appeared
in the three local Japanese newspapers on the same day, it
would appear that the information emanated from the same
source and was published without confirmation.

The local Japanese Consular Police were visited regarding
this matter when the undersigned was informed that the Japanese
authorities had also received information that the communist
leader was in Shanghai. However, the Japanese Authorities are
in possession of other information from a different source that
Chow Ung Lai is in Lushan. The Japanese Consular Police state
that so far they have received no reliable information
regarding the whereabouts of Chow Ung Lai, but in view of the
present conciliatory attitude of the Kuomintang toward the
Chinese Communist Party, it may be taken for granted that it
would not be impossible for Chow Ung Lai to pay a secret and
undetected visit to Shanghai.

Enquiries are being pursued.
Also by chinese staff.

June 18, 1937.
Afternoon Translation

The Diamond (金剛鑽) :-

REPORT OF CHINESE COMMUNIST STAYING AT BURLINGTON HOTEL
FOUND UNTRUE

Yesterday the "Shanghai Mainichi", a local
Japanese daily, published a report stating that Chow Ung-
lai (周恩來), a prominent member of the Chinese
Communist Party, had arrived in Shanghai and was staying
at the Burlington Hotel, Bubbling Well Road. The report
added that Chow Ung-lai would leave Shanghai for abroad
in company with General Yang Hu-cheng (楊虎城) on s.s.
"President Hoover" on June 29.
Acting on information contained in the above
report, a number of newspaper reporters called at the
Burlington Hotel to seek news but they could not locate
Chow Ung-lai. Subsequent enquiries made at the local
residence of General Yang Hu-Cheng and other quarters
also failed to confirm the information. After some
study, the reporters realized that the report published
in the Japanese newspaper was entirely a fabrication.

A.S. Kawashita

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, JUNE 17, 1937

Japanese Report Noted
Communist, Chou En-lai,
On Stealthy Visit Here

Red Chieftain Declared Here To Negotiate With
Kuomintang Leaders For Delegates At
National Assembly Gathering

EXTRAORDINARY PRECAUTIONS TAKEN TO
AVOID FASCIST ATTEMPT ON LIFE

Chou En-lai, the Communist leader for whose head General Chiang Kai-shek once offered $100,000, was reported yesterday by all three local Japanese newspapers to be in town.

The Vice-Chairman of the Revolutionary Military Council arrived in Shanghai "two or three days ago," these dailies said. He was stated to be a guest at the Burlington Hotel, Bubbling Well Road.

Surmises on the purpose on Mr. Chou's visit varied according to the newspapers.

The Shanghai "Mainichi" said the Red chieftain was here to continue negotiations with Nanking leaders on three points. These were given as:
1.—The appointment of eight Communist delegates to the National Assembly.
2.—The contents of a draft resolution to be jointly adopted by the various factions at the Assembly.
3.—The adoption of measures to pacify Mohammedan tribes in Sinkiang now engaged in a revolt against Soviet-backed administrators.

Visit At Kuling
Before coming here, the "Mainichi" further stated, he visited General Chiang at Kuling and also stayed for a while in Nanking. This is his second sojourn in Shanghai, the Japanese daily asserted. On his previous trip, earlier this month, he conferred with Mr. T. V. Soong, chairman of the board of directors of the Bank of China and one of the two principal negotiators in the release of General Chiang in Sian in December last year; General Yang Hu-chen, leading figure in the revolt who is now preparing to take a trip abroad, and others, the paper said.

The Shanghai "Nippo" and the Shanghai "Nichi-Nichi" linked Mr. Chou's visit to an attempt to rebuild the Chinese Communist Party.

Mr. Chou, the two dailies said in similar reports, was given a sum of money by General Chiang to proceed abroad in company with General Yang.

"He apparently has no intention of doing so," the Nichi-Nichi" said. Another rumour, reported by the two dailies, was that he would proceed to Sinkiang by air "accompanied by a well-known newspaper editor."

Fears Fascist Attempt
"Because of the fear of a Fascist attempt upon his life," the Shanghai "Nichi-Nichi" added, "Mr. Chou is registered under an assumed named and extraordinary precautions are being taken to safeguard his safety."

This is the second prominent Chinese Soviet official reported by the Japanese press to have visited Shanghai recently.

On June 5, the Japanese papers said that Chu Teh, chairman of the Revolutionary Military Council, had been a house guest at the home of General Chiang Kai-shek in the French Concession from May 26 to 28, when he had flown back to Sian. These reports lacked confirmation.

Mr. Chou, who was active in Shanghai during the Nationalist advance from Canton, studied in Japan and in Europe. He is credited with having organized the Chinese Communist League in Paris in 1923. When the Kuomintang, controlled by General Chiang, broke with the Communists in 1927, Mr. Chou joined Chu Teh and others to organize the Chinese Soviets in Kiangsi, where he became a commissar in 1931.

《字林西报》，1937年6月17日，星期四

注意到日本方面的报道
共产党人周恩来，
秘密访沪

红色首领据称在此与国民党领导人
就国民大会代表问题进行谈判

采取特别预防措施
以防法西斯分子行刺

蒋介石将军曾悬赏十万美元取其首级的共产党领袖周恩来，据当地三家日文报纸昨日报道，已在本市。

这些日报称，这位革命军事委员会副主席于“两三天前”抵达上海。据说他是静安寺路百老汇大厦的客人。

各家报纸对周先生访问目的的猜测各不相同。

上海《每日新闻》（Mainichi）称，这位红色首领来此是为了就三点问题继续与南京领导人进行谈判。这三点列为：
1.—任命八名共产党代表参加国民大会。
2.—由各方在大会上共同通过的决议草案的内容。
3.—采取的措施以平定新疆地区正在反抗苏联支持的管理者的穆斯林部落。

庐山之行
《每日新闻》进一步称，在来此之前，他曾在庐山拜访了蒋介石将军，并在南京停留了一段时间。这家日文日报断言，这是他在上海的第二次逗留。在该报称，在本月早些时候的上一次行程中，他曾与中国银行董事会主席、去年十二月西安事变中营救蒋介石将军的两名主要谈判代表之一的宋子文（T. V. Soong）先生，以及发动叛乱的关键人物、目前正准备出国旅行的杨虎臣（Yang Hu-chen）将军等人进行了会谈。

上海《日日新闻》（Nippo）和上海《日日报》（Nichi-Nichi）将周先生的访问与重建中国共产党的企图联系起来。

这两家日报在类似的报道中称，蒋介石将军给予周先生一笔款项，让他与杨将军一同出国。

“他显然无意这样做，”《日日报》说。这两家日报报道的另一则谣言是，他将乘飞机前往新疆，“由一位知名报纸编辑陪同”。

担心法西斯分子行刺
上海《日日报》补充道：“由于担心法西斯分子对其生命进行暗杀，周先生使用化名登记，并采取了非凡的预防措施以保障其安全。”

这是日本媒体近期报道的第二位访问上海的中共苏维埃高级官员。

6月5日，日本报纸称，革命军事委员会主席朱德曾于5月26日至28日作为客人住在法租界蒋介石将军的家中，随后飞回西安。这些报道缺乏证实。

周先生在国民党从广州北进期间活跃于上海，曾在日本和欧洲留学。据信他于1923年在巴黎组织了中国共产主义青年团。当由蒋介石控制的国民党于1927年与共产党决裂时，周先生加入朱德等人，在江西组织中国苏维埃，并于1931年在那里担任政委。

June 26, 1937 THE CHINA WEEKLY REVIEW

Communist Leader Arrives in Shanghai to
Re-establish Party

The Shanghai Nippo June 22 stated that since the secret penetration into Shanghai of Chow En-lai, noted Communist chief, the movement for the reestablishment of the Chinese Communist Party has been tactfully expanded. Upon the secret instructions given by Chow En-lai, his followers allegedly commenced their activities in the establishment of the branch headquarters of the Chinese Communist Party in various local universities and colleges in collaboration with the United Student National Salvation Associations in these different educational institutions. About a week ago, Mr. Chow had a conference with representatives of the national salvation associations of the students in a Peking restaurant on Foochow Road, at which a decision was reached, among others, to demand the revision of the regulations governing the election of representatives to the National People's Congress.

GEN. CHIANG'S SON AND CHOW EN-LAI ALLEGEDLY
CONFERRING ON REBUILDING OF RED PARTY

Chiang Ching-kuo, son of General Chiang Kai-shek, who recently returned from a period of study in Russia, is conferring with Chow En-lai, vice-chairman of the Revolutionary Military Council of the Chinese Soviet, regarding means to rebuild a legalized Chinese Communist Party, according to a report published in the Shanghai Mainichi, June 17. The reorganized Communist party, the Mainichi said, would be radically different from that which created the Chinese Soviet Government in Juikin, Kiangsi, and would abandon the tenets that it advertised previous to the Sian coup of Dec. 12 last year. "Gen. Chiang feels," the paper continued, "that so long as the Communist party intends to go along with the Kuomintang in creating a new nation, there are no grounds for opposition. "He appears to be of the opinion that two great parties can exist side by side in the manner followed by other democratic nations," the Japanese daily asserted. Chow, who was said to have flown to Kuling in company with "another Communist," is endeavoring to rebuild the Communist party so that it would not have to bow to the dictates of the Kuomintang at the National People's Congress on Nov. 12 this year, according to the Mainichi. Unless they regain their strength by then, the paper pointed out, the Reds would be heavily outnumbered by the Nationalists. Other subjects being discussed between Chow and the Generalissimo, the journal added, included the selection of Communist delegates to Congress, the adoption of a joint resolution by all factions and the pacification of revolting Mohammedans in Sinkiang.

Chow En-lai

1937年6月26日 《密勒氏评论报》（THE CHINA WEEKLY REVIEW）

共产党领袖抵沪
重建政党

6月22日《上海日日新闻》（Shanghai Nippo）称，自从著名共产党首领周恩来秘密潜入上海以来，重建中国共产党的运动已策略性地扩大。据称，在周恩来的秘密指示下，其追随者开始与各教育机构的全国学生救国联合会合作，在各大学院校建立中国共产党分支总部。约一周前，周先生在福州路的一家北京餐馆与学生救国会代表举行会议，会上达成多项决定，其中包括要求修改国民代表大会代表选举条例。

据称蒋中正之子
与周恩来就重建红色政党进行会谈

据6月17日《上海每日新闻》（Shanghai Mainichi）刊登的一篇报道，刚从俄国留学归来的蒋介石将军之子蒋经国，正与中国苏维埃革命军事委员会副主席周恩来就重建合法化的中国共产党的方法进行会谈。《每日新闻》称，重组后的共产党将与在江西瑞金创建中华苏维埃政府的共产党截然不同，并将放弃其在去年12月12日西安事变之前所宣扬的主张。该报继续称：“蒋将军认为，只要共产党打算与国民党共同建设一个新国家，就没有反对的理由。”这家日文日报断言：“他似乎认为，两大政党可以像其他民主国家那样并存。”据《每日新闻》称，据说与“另一名共产党人”一同飞往庐山的周恩来，正努力重建共产党，使其不必在今年11月12日的国民代表大会上屈从于国民党的指令。该报指出，除非到那时他们能恢复实力，否则红军在人数上将远少于国民党。该刊补充道，周与委员长讨论的其他议题还包括挑选共产党出席大会的代表、通过各方联合决议以及平定新疆叛乱的穆斯林。

周恩来

NIPPO

CHINESE STUDENTS ACTIVE TO REORGANIZE COMMUNIST PARTY

Since the arrival of the communist
leader, Chow Ung-lai, in Shanghai Chinese communists are
active towards re-establishing the communist party. The
communist organizers, who have received a secret order
from Chow Ung-lai to re-organize the communist party, are
active among the students' national salvation associations
of various universities.

About a week ago the United
University Students' National Salvation Association held a
meeting of representatives of various students' national
salvation associations at a certain Peiping restaurant on
Foochow Road and discussed ways and means for future
propaganda. The following resolutions were passed:-
1. That the movement for the release of the seven
arrested popular front leaders be accelerated.
2. That the regulations governing the elections of
representatives to the National Assembly be revised and that
students be given the right of voting.
It is noteworthy that a large
number of girl students attended the meeting.

《日日新闻》（NIPPO）

中国学生积极重组共产党

自共产党领袖周恩来（Chow Ung-lai）抵达上海以来，中国共产党人正积极致力于重建共产党。收到周恩来秘密命令以重组共产党的共产党组织者，在各大学的学生救国联合会中活动频繁。

约一周前，全国大学生救国联合会在福州路某家北京餐馆举行了各学生救国联合会代表会议，讨论了未来宣传的方式方法。通过了以下决议：-
1. 加速释放被捕的七位人民阵线领导人的运动。
2. 修改国民大会代表选举条例，并给予学生投票权。
值得注意的是，大量女学生参加了此次会议。

COMMUNIST LEADER MEETS MADAME CHIANG KAI-SHEK
IN SHANGHAI

It is reported that Chu Teh,
chairman of the Red Army Affairs Committee, arrived in
Shanghai on Wednesday last and held a conference with
Madame Chiang Kai-shek at the latter's home. During the
conference he informed Madame Chiang of the Red Army
situation and the result of the co-operation between the
National Government and the Communist Party. It is said
that there are 100,000 Red soldiers in Shensi, Kansu,
Hunan and Szechuen Provinces. Chu Teh left again for
Sian on Saturday.

The C.C. Corps at Sian murdered
two body guards of Chow Ung-lai during an attempt on the
life of the latter. For this reason, the Nanking Government
is perturbed about the activities of the C. C. Corps.

共产党领袖在上海
会见蒋宋美龄夫人

据报道，红军事务委员会主席朱德于上周三抵达上海，并在蒋宋美龄夫人家中与其举行会谈。会谈期间，他向蒋夫人通报了红军的情况以及国民政府与共产党合作的结果。据说在陕西、甘肃、湖南和四川省有十万红军士兵。朱德于周六再次离开前往西安。

西安的CC系人员在试图暗杀周恩来（Chow Ung-lai）的过程中杀害了他的两名保镖。因此，南京政府对CC系人员的活动感到不安。

Following their expulsion from the Central Provinces of
China the Chinese red armies moved up into the West and North-
west where the barren and inaccessible nature of the country
curtailed their food and ammunition supplies, thus considerably
weakening the morale of the forces.

Soviet Russia, seeking to strengthen her position in
relation to China and at the same time watchful of Japan's
increasing influence in the Far East, made a proposal to
General Chiang Kai Shek suggesting that Russia would assist
China in her efforts to organize a strong Central Government
if China, for her part, would incorporate the Chinese Com-
munist Party with the Kuomintang.

In spite of the efforts of Marshal Chang Hsueh Liang,
whose troops were in close proximity to end friendly with
the Red armies, to persuade him to accept this proposal,
General Chiang refused and continued with his bandit suppression
campaign.

With the occurrence of the Sian incident, however, a
change in the situation took place and General Chiang promised
his kidnappers that he would reconsider the question pertain-
ing to the Red armies and endeavour to arrange an amicable
settlement.

苏联俄罗斯寻求加强其对华地位，同时警惕日本在远东日益增长的影响力，向蒋介石将军提出建议，表示如果中国方面将中国共产党并入国民党，俄罗斯将协助中国努力组建一个强大的中央政府。

In compliance with the instructions of the D.C. (Special
Branch) on the attached report, I have to state that further
enquiries have been made regarding the problem of reconciliation
between the Chinese Republic Special Area Government (until
recently known as the Chinese Soviet Republic) and the National
Government, and the following is a resume of the circumstances
surrounding the proposed amalgamation of these two bodies:

The proposed reconciliation was initiated in February
1936 when the Chinese Communist Party distributed a circular
letter to political parties, military units and the masses
throughout the country urging all parties to unite against
Japan. Simultaneously, another circular letter was addressed
by the Chinese Red Army to commanders of the various Government
military units, including Gen. Chiang Kai Shek, suggesting
that a conference of Government and Communist Militarists be
convened to discuss the formation of an anti-Japanese army,
comprised of Government and Communist soldiers.

In pursuance of its new policy of effecting a cessation
of civil strife and of forming an "Anti-Japanese United Front",
the Chinese Communist Party expressed its willingness to
abolish the Chinese Soviet Republic and to place the Red Army
under the control of a Military Affairs Commission in which
the Communists would be given proportionate representation.
The Government authorities, however, doubted the sincerity
of the Chinese Communist Party and consequently paid no heed
to the proposal.

ciliation has met with unqualified success, but it is generally

During the month of November 1936, Gen. Chiang Kai Shek
tried to bring pressure on the military units in Shensi to
extend their anti-bandit campaign, but the latter, in view
of their partial reconciliation with the Communist Party,
were unwilling to renew hostilities with the Reds. This
refusal resulted in the Young Marshal's invitation to Gen.
Chiang Kai Shek to give an instructive lecture to the former's
troops at Sian. The Generalissimo accepted the invitation
and, despite the negative advice of his loyal subordinates,
proceeded to the Shensi capital, where the young officers of
the aforementioned armies brought about the Sian Coup d'etat
which resulted in the detention of Gen. Chiang and a number
of prominent Government officials.

There are indications that during the negotiations which
followed, the eight demands submitted by the mutineers for
the release of the Generalissimo and his entourage, were accepted
and endorsed by Mr. T.V. Soong, but with the refusal of the
Nanking authorities to countenance acceptance of these demands,
the general situation at once assumed a more serious aspect ASPECT
and hostilities between the two parties seemed imminent.
The peace-loving faction of the Nanking Government, however,
succeeded in checking the hasty decision of the Government
radicals and the release of the Generalissimo was obtained
after further negotiations.

illness of Gen. Chiang Kai Shek, an expeditious settlement
of the problem appears doubtful.

Made by D.I. Kuh Pao Hwa Forwarded by J. Boyne O.S.I.

With reference to the attached newspaper report to the
effect that the Chinese Communist Party in the North-West
has accepted the measures drawn up by the Kuomintang Third
Plenary Session, that all the Red forces be reorganized and
placed under the control of the Military Affairs Commission
at Nanking, that Party leaders including Gen. Chu Teh and
Gen. Mao Shih Tung will voluntarily dissolve their Soviet
Government and cease their Red propaganda, I have to state
that this information lacks confirmation. The report probably
arises out of the following circumstances:-

Prior to the convention of the Third Plenary Session,
advance information was obtained by the Communist Party to the
effect that the Kuomintang would move a proposition to the
Congress to the effect that no rival government be allowed to
exist as long as the Central Government remains in power,
otherwise it would amount to an open challenge to the existence
of the National Government. Being aware of what was likely to
transpire, the Communist Party at about the same time as the
Third Plenary Session was convened, declared that the Red Army
would henceforth be known as the "Anti-Japanese Revolutionary
Army" (抗日革命军), while the Soviet area would be termed the
"Practical Land Test Area" (土地实验区). The change of the
nomenclature of the Red Army is in accordance with the Anti-
Japanese United Front Policy of the Communist Party and is
intended to clearly indicate to the masses the objective of
this army. The functions of the Red Army, however, still
remain unchanged.

by the Communist Party of the measures drawn up by the Third

Hwa Mei Wan Pao dated March 4 :-

RED ARMY TO BE REORGANIZED BY NANKING

According to reliable information, the
Communist Party in the North-West has accepted all the measures
for their surrender as drawn up at the Third Plenary Session
of the Kuomintang. All the Red forces under the Communist
Party will be reorganized by the Central authorities and will
be placed under the control of the Military Affairs Commission,
while the leaders of the Communist Party like Chu Teh and
Mao Tse Tung will voluntarily dissolve their Soviet Government

After they have given up their military and political work,
these leaders will be sent abroad.
It is learnt that the Communist Party has
already started to make arrangements with the Central author-
ities to carry out the arrangements. The Central Government
has already sent an important official to the North-West to
handle the negotiations.

MAINICHI 9.3.37.
CO-OPERATION BET EEN NANKING GOVERNMENT
AND COMMUNIST PARTY

The Mainichi publishes the
following leading article:-
As a result of the Third
Plenary Session the Nanking Government is reported to
have decided to bring about a change of the Japanese,
German and Italian Ambassadors to China as the first
step to be adopted against the joint defence policy adopted
by these three countries.
Japan had proposed co-operation
with China against the communists for the safety of the
Far East, but the Government and the people of China
misunderstood Japan's motives and charged Japan with
being an aggressor. The co-operation must deal with
the Chinese communist party and the red army but its
motive is to put a check to the Soviet's advance and
influence. Should China co-operate with the communists
the anti-communist campaign will become a serious question
for Japan.
The Chinese communist party
may cease its anti-Chiang Kai Shek and anti-Nanking
Government activities in return for Nanking's co-operation.
The communist party will then play a great part in China's
politics and Soviet Russia will derive much benefit
because the Comintern will be pulling the strings behind
the scenes. The temporary inactivity of the communists
is a part of their tactics, they will never co-operate
to support a government of capitalists and imperialists.
pages.zh:
《每日新闻》1937年3月9日。
南京政府与共产党之合作

《每日新闻》发表如下社论：
据报，鉴于第三次全体会议的结果，南京政府已决定更换日本、德国及意大利驻华大使，以此作为针对上述三国所采取的联合防御政策的第一步措施。
日本曾提议与中国合作反共，以保障远东安全，但中国政府与民众误解了日本的动机，指责日本为侵略者。此种合作必须涉及中国共产党与红军，但其目的在于遏制苏联的扩张及其影响。若中国与共产党合作，反共运动将成为日本面临的严重问题。
作为对南京方面合作的回报，中国共产党可能会停止其反蒋介石及反南京政府的活动。此后，共产党将在中国政治中发挥重要作用，而苏俄将因此获益良多，因为共产国际将在幕后操纵一切。共产党的暂时不活动是其策略的一部分，他们绝不会合作支持一个资本家与帝国主义的政府。

pages.en:
MA NICH I
RELEASE OF CHIANG KAI SHEK EFFECTED BY COMMUNIST
LEADER

A special telegram from Nanking
reports that serious attention is being paid to the
activities of the red troops in Kansu and Shensi Provinces
as it is likely to cause international complications
between Japan, Manchukuo, China and Soviet Russia. After
the Sian incident the National Government completely
ceased its anti-communist campaign. Furthermore the
Kuomintang and the Communist Party are coming closer
together after Nanking reached a compromise with the
forces of General Chang Hsueh Liang and General Yang
Hu Chung. Co-operation between the National Government
and the Communist Party is approaching.
Chow Ing Lai, a leader of the
Communist Party, who rendered great service in the release
of General Chiang Kai Shek from Sian, negotiated with
General Chiang Kai Shek at Fenghua for the unification of
the Kuomintang and the Communist Party. This question
was heatedly debated at the Third Plenary Session. As
a result, four conditions were drawn up for co-operation
between the National Government and the Communist Party.
Mr. Cheng Chong, member of the C.E.C., was dispatched to
Shensi to conduct the negotiations with communists.
Eventually the communist party accepted the conditions
and it was decided to carry out the following four measures:-
1. That the Chinese Soviet Government be cancelled;
that the Nanking Government be recognized as a united
government and the central authority of anti-Japanese
organizations; that positive support be given to the
Nanking Government.
2. That the title of red army be abolished and
be put under the control of the Military Affairs Commission.
3. That all communistic propaganda and anti-Nanking
Government activities be suppressed.
4. That class struggle be abandoned.
pages.zh:
《每日新闻》
蒋介石之获释系由共产党领袖促成

来自南京的特电报道，甘肃与陕西省红军部队的活动正受到密切关注，因其可能引发日本、满洲国、中国与苏俄之间的国际纠纷。西安事变后，国民政府完全停止了反共运动。此外，在南京与张学良将军及杨虎城将军的部队达成妥协后，国民党与共产党之间的关系日益密切。国民政府与共产党之间的合作正在逼近。
在西安事变中为释放蒋介石将军立下大功的共产党领导人周英来（音译），在奉化与蒋介石将军就国共统一问题进行谈判。此议题在第三次全体会议上引发了激烈辩论。结果，拟定了国民政府与共产党合作的四项条件。中央执行委员会成员程冲（音译）被派往陕西与共产党进行谈判。最终，共产党接受了这些条件，并决定实施以下四项措施：
1. 取消中华苏维埃政府；承认南京政府为统一政府及抗日组织的中央权威；给予南京政府积极支持。
2. 废除红军番号，将其置于军事委员会的控制之下。
3. 取缔所有共产主义宣传及反南京政府的活动。
4. 放弃阶级斗争。

February 24, 1937. Afternoon Translation.
Hwa Tung Ya Pao dated February 23 (Nanking Telegram):-
THE COMMUNISTS AND THE NANKING GOVERNMENT
Following the peaceful settlement of the Shensi trouble, the red bandits, taught by their bitter experiences during the past few years and now fully realizing the favourable tendency of the people towards the National Government, are contemplating surrender to the Nanking Government. As a matter of fact, they are already contemplating disbandment. When the Third Plenary Session was in progress at Nanking, the communist bandits conducted extensive propaganda regarding their surrender to the National Government. They advocated the concentration of the whole strength of the nation for resistance against XX.
The National Government resolved to give the communists a chance for repentance. It is learned that the communist party, with a view to proving its sincerely, has announced the severance of its connection with the Third Internationale.

2月23日《华东雅报》（南京电）：
共产党与南京政府
继陕西事态和平解决后，赤匪从过去几年的痛苦经历中吸取教训，并充分认识到民众倾向国民政府的有利态势，正考虑向南京政府投降。事实上，他们已在考虑解散队伍。当第三次全体会议在南京进行时，共匪就其向国民政府投降一事进行了大规模宣传。他们主张集中全国力量抵抗 XX。

Feb. 22. 37.    THE THIRD PLENARY SESSION    229U

The Mainichi publishes the
following leading article:-
    The Third Plenary Session closed
yesterday after discussing the communist problem. The
important proposals submitted to the Session and the
results of the discussions have not been made public.
    The three proposals reported
to have been submitted to the Session by Sian and the
other proposals reported to have been submitted by
General Feng Yu Hsiang, General Li Lieh Chun, Madame
Sun Yat Sen and General Chang Chun have not been made
public.    The anti-Japanese proposals and the result of
the pro-communist discussion are being kept secret. In
the declaration issued by the Third Plenary Session no
mention was made of the anti-Japanese policy, but pro-
European and pro-American intentions were expressed.
    Mr. Chang Chi, an elder statesman,
strongly advocated a great change in China's policy
towards Japan.    It is said that no change will be made
in the anti-communist campaign, but General Chiang Kai
Shek purposely read the eight demands submitted by Sian
at the Third Plenary Session and requested a discussion.
Thus General Chiang Kai Shek has fulfilled his promise
made at Sian, but it cannot be said that the proposal
has been accepted, as General Chiang Kai Shek's anti-
communist policy has been changed and the campaign has
now ceased.    The important business of the Session
was to deal with the Sian incident, but the Sian demands
have been neither accepted nor rejected. As regards
anti-Japanese policy, no definite decision has been
reached.    All problems still remain unsolved.

1937年2月22日。    第三次全体会议    229U

《每日新闻》发表如下社论：
第三次全体会议在讨论共产党问题后于昨日闭幕。提交会议的重要提案及讨论结果尚未公布。
据报由西安方面提交的三项提案，以及据报由冯玉祥将军、李烈钧将军、孙逸仙夫人及张群将军提交的其他提案，均未公开。反日提案及亲共讨论的结果均被保密。在第三次全体会议发表的宣言中，未提及反日政策，但表达了亲欧及亲美的意向。
元老张继先生强烈主张改变中国的对日政策。据说反共运动不会有所改变，但蒋介石将军故意在第三次全体会议上宣读了西安方面提出的八项要求，并要求进行讨论。因此，蒋介石将军履行了他在西安作出的承诺，但不能说该提案已被接受，因为蒋介石将军的反共政策已发生改变，且运动现已停止。会议的重要议程是处理西安事变，但西安方面的要求既未被接受也未被拒绝。关于反日政策，尚未作出明确决定。所有问题仍未解决。

February 22, 1937.
Afternoon Translation.

Crystal (晶報) publishes the following article:

NANKING GOVERNMENT AND THE COMMUNISTS

According to a person arriving here from Shensi,
the Communists in Shensi and Kansu Provinces have completely
come to their senses. On February 10 they informed the
Third Internationale of their severance from the Communist
Party.

Meanwhile, the Communists have made known
in a written declaration five points, three of which are as
follows:-
1) The Soviet organizations of Communists in the five North-
west provinces, namely, Sinkiang, Kansu, Shensi, Tsinghai
and Ninghsia will be abolished.
2) The comrades in the North-west will unanimously accept
the guidance of the Chinese Kuomintang and obey the orders
of the Central military authorities at Nanking.
3) The policy of incendiarism, massacre of people, landlords
and capitalists and immorality will be abandoned.

The Communists are ready to surrender to the
Nanking Government. It is understood that the Central
authorities will conduct a careful study into the matter and
will probably accept the Communists on certain conditions.

南京政府与共产党

据一位从陕西抵达此处的人士称，陕西与甘肃省的共产党人已完全清醒。2月10日，他们通知第三国际其与共产党断绝关系。

同时，共产党在一项书面声明中公布了五点内容，其中三点如下：
1) 废除共产党在西北五省，即新疆、甘肃、陕西、青海及宁夏的苏维埃组织。
2) 西北地区的同志将一致接受中国国民党的领导，并服从南京中央军事当局的命令。
3) 放弃纵火、屠杀人民、地主及资本家以及不道德行为的政策。

共产党准备向南京政府投降。据悉，中央当局将对此事进行仔细研究，并可能在某些条件下接受共产党。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, MONDAY, FEBRUARY 22, 1937
19411

Complete Recantation Of
Red Tenets Asked Before
Reconciliation Possible

C. E. C. Makes Known Conditions Precedent To Any
Dealings By Nanking With Communist Element,
Whose List Of Crimes Are Enumerated

IMPORTANT RESOLUTION PASSED AT
THIRD PLENARY SESSION

NANKING, Feb. 21.—Complete recantation of Communistic doctrines and abolition of the Red Army and Government are first conditions which are held absolutely necessary for a reconciliation with the Communist-bandits, according to an important resolution passed by the sixth general meeting of the Executive Committee of the Fifth Kuomintang Central Executive Committee.

Until and unless the Communist-bandits sincerely repent their past mistakes, obey the Three People's Principles, abide by the nation's laws and strictly adhere to military discipline, there could be no question of the Central Government again taking them into its fold, the resolution declared.

The resolution, which was moved by the Presidium, listed four major conditions under which the Central authorities would be prepared to effect a reconciliation with the Red bandits who have during the last decade been such a disturbing factor in China's internal stability and peace. These four conditions are:

First, abolition of the Red Army and its incorporation into the unified command of the nation's armed forces;

Second, unification of Government power in the hands of the Central Government, and dissolution of the so-called "Chinese Soviet Republic" and other organizations detrimental to Government unity;

Third, absolute cessation of Communistic propaganda, which is diametrically opposed to the Three People's Principles; and

Fourth, stoppage of class struggle which splits society into antagonistic classes and invites mutual destruction.

History Of Communism

The resolution, which was received by the plenum with acclaim, first gives a brief account of the Communists in Chinese politics.

When Communists were individually admitted by the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen into the Kuomintang in 1924, the resolution states, promise was given that they would work for China's national revolution. Not only did they not keep their promise, but they actually worked for the splitting of the Kuomintang.

At the beginning, the Kuomintang, always lenient and tolerant, had hoped that they would soon wake up to their mistakes and make amends for their misdeeds.

The hopes of the Kuomintang, however, were doomed to disappointment. After the Nationalist Forces had taken Hankow and Changsha in Hunan, in 1926, and later extended their occupation to the Wuhan Area, the Communist elements tried to sever the ties between the Kuomintang and the masses.

Alongside with these subversive activities, the Communists propagated Red theories and worked for the downfall of the revolutionary and national reconstruction movement led by the Kuomintang. They also tried their best to hinder the eastward advance of the Nationalist Forces against Shanghai and Nanking as well as the northward march on Chengchow and Loyang.

Besides, they were also responsible for the reign of terror in Hunan and Hupeh, and caused a division between Nanking and Hankow. Because of the Communists' anti-revolutionary activities, the Northern Expedition almost came to a standstill.

Class War Incited

Later, the Communists openly organized the Chinese Red Army and demoralized the basic structure of the Kuomintang. They incited class warfare in the hope to seize governing power.

In order to consolidate the foundation of the Party, to carry the Northern Expedition to a successful conclusion and to save the people from suffering, the Kuomintang came upon a momentous decision to purge its rank and file of Communistic elements.

After that, for more than 10 years, the Communists continued their propaganda among the people and created disturbances at various provinces, including Kiangsi, Kwangtung, Fukien, Chekiang, Hunan, and Szechwan.

Echo Of Year 1931

These, the resolution points out, are facts which need no enumeration. The crowning crime of the Communist-bandits, however, was what they had done since September, 1931, when China was plunged into a grave national crisis.

Taking advantage of the Government's preoccupation with the external menace, the Communists attacked Kangchow in Kiangsi during the Shanghai War. Later during hostilities along the Great Wall in 1933 they attacked Fuchow and menaced Nanchang. In both cases they hindered the free movement of Government troops for national defence.

Now having been driven to the Northwestern corner of the country, where livelihood is difficult and where foodstuffs are scarce, the Communist-bandits began to spread reports of their alleged willingness to surrender.

The resolution then says: With universal brotherhood at heart, the Kuomintang is not disposed to deprive any people of a chance to reform and start life anew. However, in view of their past deceit and the pitfalls which the Kuomintang had previously fallen into, it must not repeat its mistakes again.

The resolution then enumerates the four major conditions absolutely necessary before the Party will consider a reconciliation with the Reds.

The resolution in conclusion declares that no nation on earth can tolerate the existence within its territory of any organization which is detrimental to the interests of the State and the whole people, and which depends on external forces for its activities. For preservation of the last glory of the Republic and consummation of the Three People's Principles, the Red scourge must be annihilated root and branch.—Central News.

General Exodus

NANKING, Feb. 21.—A general exodus of C.E.C. members who have been gathering here to attend the Third Plenary Session of the Fifth Central Executive Committee of the Kuomintang during the past seven days, will begin immediately after its closing ceremony tomorrow morning.

Called by business, several of the members have left Nanking today. Among them were Mr. T. V. Soong, member of the Standing Committee of the National Economic Council, who flew to Shanghai this noon, and General Huang Shao-hsiung, Chairman of the Hupeh Provincial Government, who took off by plane for Hankow this afternoon.—Central News.

Plenary Session To Adjourn

NANKING, Feb. 21.—The Third Plenary Session of the Fifth Kuomintang C. E. C., which has been in session during the past week, will formally adjourn tomorrow morning when a lengthy manifesto will be issued.

Several important changes in the personnel of the Central Party Headquarters were announced at the sixth general session this afternoon.

Mr. Chen Li-fu, former Minister of Education, was appointed Head of the Organization Department, replacing Mr. Chang Tao-fan, who has resigned his position.

Mr. Shao Li-tzu, former Minister of Communications, was appointed...

19411

在实现和解之前
要求彻底放弃红色信条

中央执行委员会公布南京方面与共产党势力进行任何交涉的先决条件，并列举其罪状

第三次全体会议通过重要决议

南京，2月21日电。——据中国国民党第五届中央执行委员会第六次全体会议通过的一项重要决议，彻底放弃共产主义教义以及废除红军和苏维埃政府，被视为与“共匪”和解的绝对必要的首要条件。

该决议宣称，除非“共匪”真诚悔悟过往错误，服从三民主义，遵守国家法律并严格遵守军纪，否则中央政府绝无可能再次将其纳入体制之内。

这项由主席团提出的决议，列出了中央当局准备与过去十年间严重扰乱中国内部稳定与和平的“赤匪”实现和解的四个主要条件。这四个条件是：

第一，废除红军，并将其编入国家武装力量的统一指挥体系；

第二，将政府权力统一于中央政府手中，解散所谓的“中华苏维埃共和国”及其他有损政府统一的组织；

第三，绝对停止与三民主义背道而驰的共产主义宣传；

第四，停止将社会分裂为对立阶级并导致相互毁灭的阶级斗争。

共产主义历史

该决议首先简要回顾了共产主义者在中国政治中的活动，并在全体会议上获得热烈拥护。

决议指出，1924年，已故孙中山博士个别接纳共产主义者加入国民党时，他们曾承诺致力于中国的国民革命。然而，他们不仅未信守承诺，反而实际上致力于分裂国民党。

起初，国民党始终秉持宽厚容忍的态度，希望他们能很快醒悟自身错误，并为不当行为做出补救。

然而，国民党的希望注定落空。1926年，当国民革命军占领湖南的汉口和长沙，随后又将占领区扩展至武汉地区时，共产党势力试图切断国民党与民众之间的联系。

在进行这些颠覆活动的同时，共产主义者传播红色理论，致力于推翻由国民党领导的革命与国家建设运动。他们还极力阻碍国民革命军向上海和南京的东进，以及向郑州和洛阳的北伐。

此外，他们还应对湖南和湖北的恐怖统治负责，并造成了南京与汉口之间的分裂。由于共产主义者的反革命活动，北伐战争几乎陷入停滞。

煽动阶级战争

后来，共产主义者公开组建了中国红军，并从内部瓦解了国民党的基本结构。他们煽动阶级战争，企图夺取执政权。

为了巩固党的基础，顺利完成北伐，并使人民免受苦难，国民党做出了清除党内共产主义分子的重大决定。

此后十余年间，共产主义者继续在民众中进行宣传，并在江西、广东、福建、浙江、湖南和四川等各省制造动乱。

1931年的回响

决议指出，这些都是无需赘述的事实。然而，“共匪”最大的罪行发生在1931年9月之后，当时中国陷入了严重的民族危机。

利用政府忙于应对外部威胁之机，共产主义者在淞沪抗战期间袭击了江西的赣州。后来在1933年长城沿线战事期间，他们袭击福州并威胁南昌。在这两次事件中，他们都阻碍了政府军队为国防目的的自由调动。

如今，已被驱赶至国家西北角落的“共匪”，面对生计艰难、食物匮乏的局面，开始散布其所谓愿意投降的消息。

决议随后表示：国民党本着天下大同的精神，不愿剥夺任何人改过自新、重新开始生活的机会。然而，鉴于他们过去的欺骗行为以及国民党此前曾落入的陷阱，绝不能再重蹈覆辙。

决议随后列举了在党考虑与“赤色分子”和解之前绝对必要的四个主要条件。

决议最后声明，世界上没有任何国家能够容忍在其领土内存在任何损害国家和全体人民利益、并依靠外部势力进行活动的组织。为了维护民国的最后荣耀并实现三民主义，必须彻底根除红色祸患。——中央通讯社。

大规模离京

南京，2月21日电。——过去七天聚集在此参加国民党第五届中央执行委员会第三次全体会议的中央执行委员会委员们，将在明天上午闭幕式结束后立即开始大规模离开。

因公务在身，几名委员今日已离开南京。其中包括国民经济委员会常务委员宋子文先生，他于今日中午飞抵上海；以及湖北省政府主席黄绍竑将军，他于今日下午乘飞机前往汉口。——中央通讯社。

全体会议即将休会

南京，2月21日电。——过去一周一直开会的国民党第五届中央执行委员会第三次全体会议，将于明天上午正式休会，届时将发布一份长篇宣言。

今天下午举行的第六次全体会议上宣布了对党中央总部人事的几项重要变动。

前教育部长陈立夫先生被任命为组织部部长，接替已辞职的张道藩先生。

前交通部长邵力子先生被任命……

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, FEBRUARY 21, 1937

Nanking's Possible Offer
To Communist Party

Important Resolution To Be Discussed At Final
C.E.C. Meeting To-day; Outline Of Terms In
Resolution; Propaganda Must Be Ended

NANKING, Feb. 20.—The third plenary session of the Central Executive and Central Control committees decided this morning to convene a National People's congress on November 12.
A manifesto on the conference, which will be issued to-morrow, will give:
1.—A detailed explanation of the Kuomintang's foreign policy and will outline the general policy by which the Chinese government will conduct foreign relations.
2.—It will explain the purpose and functions of the National People's Congress and will express the determination of the Kuomintang to suppress the Communists in China through China's own efforts.
3.—It will stress the necessity of improving the economic conditions of the people and developing China's resources.
The proposal made by the Chinese Communist Party for co-operation with the Kuomintang and the National Government will be discussed at the concluding meeting of the conference to-morrow afternoon.

Terms To Communists
A resolution on the following lines will, it is learned, be submitted:
That the proposed co-operation of the Communists be accepted only on the following conditions:
1.—The Chinese Red Army is to be abolished, and the forces comprising it made part of the National Army under officers appointed by the military authorities.
2.—The Chinese Soviet Government is to be abolished and all organizations now under its control shall be under the authority and orders of the National Government.
3.—The Chinese Communist Party shall not spread communistic propaganda.
The resolution, which, it is predicted, will be adopted, will further provide for the continuance of the anti-Communist campaign if the conditions laid down are not accepted.—Reuter.

《上海星期日报》，1937年2月21日

南京可能向共产党提出的提议

重要决议将于今日中央执行委员会最后一次会议上讨论；决议条款概要；必须停止宣传

南京，2月20日电。——中央执行委员会和中央监察委员会第三次全体会议今晨决定于11月12日召开国民大会。
明日发布的关于此次会议的宣言将包含以下内容：
1. 详细解释国民党的外交政策，并概述中国政府处理对外关系的一般方针。
2. 解释国民大会的目的和职能，并表达国民党通过中国自身努力镇压国内共产主义者的决心。
3. 强调改善人民经济状况和发展中国资源的必要性。
中国共产党提出的与国民党及国民政府合作的提议，将在明天下午的会议闭幕会上进行讨论。

对共产党的条件

据悉，将提交一项大致如下的决议：
仅在满足以下条件的前提下，才接受共产党提出的合作建议：
1. 废除中国红军，其所属部队成为国民军的一部分，军官由军事当局任命。
2. 废除中华苏维埃政府，目前受其控制的所有组织均须服从国民政府的权威和命令。
3. 中国共产党不得传播共产主义宣传。
据预测将获得通过的该决议还将规定，如果上述条件不被接受，将继续进行反共运动。——路透社。

February 20, 1937. Morning Translation.

Shanghai Evening News (大晚晚报) published the following
report on February 19 :-

MADAME SUN YAT SEN SUBMITS A SUGGESTION TO THE THIRD
PLENARY SESSION FOR RESISTANCE TO JAPAN

On the morning of February 18, Madame Sun
Yat Sen issued from her residence in the French Concession
a written statement to which was attached a suggestion
that she had submitted to the Third Plenary Session of
the Kuomintang at Nanking.
In this suggestion, she advocates a "united
front" for the salvation of the nation. This suggestion
also bears the signatures of General Feng Yu Hsiang,
Mr. Sun Fo, Mr. Chang Ching Kiang, General Li Lieh Chun,
General Lu Chung Lin and eight other members of the C.E.C.
of the Kuomintang.
The following is the proposal submitted by
Madame Sun Yat Sen to the Third Plenary Session of the
Kuomintang :-
"At this time of national crisis, the eyes
of the people are turned upon the Third Plenary Session.
China has reached the final stage in enduring Japan's
invasions and is prepared to make the last sacrifice.
The provoking attitude of the Japanese has caused the
anti-Japanese movement in China to become more vigorous.
Japan's plot to seize North China will never be successful.
The activities of the Japanese and the bandits in invading
Suiyuan have failed because of the resistance put up by
the Chinese soldiers. The oppression of China by Japan
will also meet with failure. The determination of the
Chinese people to make no further concessions to Japan
and their preparations to recover lost territories are
full of significance.
"It is most unfortunate that certain
politicians have as yet a vague understanding of these
conditions and have sacrificed China because of their
fear of Japan. These politicians pay too much attention
to the strength of Japan and belittle the strength of
the Chinese people.
"These are the reasons why Japan can never
overcome China :-
1) The financial power of Japan is weak; she is not in
a position to maintain war for any long period of time.
2) The Japanese people are opposed to war and are
dissatisfied with the dangerous policy adopted by
their militarists.
3) There are defects in Japan's military plans, while her
tactics are not modern.
4) The Chinese people are determined to offer resistance
to the bitter end.
"The position of Japan in the Far East
is so unsatisfactory that she cannot dispatch even 20
Divisions to fight China. Even if Japan can send 20
Divisions, it will not be sufficient, for the well-trained
Chinese forces that are scattered in different parts of
the country are prepared to sacrifice their lives for the
nation.

1937年2月20日。晨间译件。

《大晚晚报》于2月19日刊登了以下
报道：

孙逸仙夫人向第三次全体会议提交抗日建议

2月18日上午，孙逸仙夫人从其在法租界的寓所
发布了一份书面声明，附上了她已向在南京召开的
国民党第三次全体会议提交的一项建议。
在这项建议中，她主张建立救国“统一
战线”。该建议上还签有冯玉祥将军、
孙佛先生、张静江先生、李烈钧将军、
陆仲林将军以及国民党其他八名中央执行委
员的名字。
以下是孙逸仙夫人向国民党第三次全体
会议提交的提案：
“值此民族危机之际，民众的目光聚焦于
第三次全体会议。中国忍受日本侵略已达最后阶
段，并准备做出最后的牺牲。日本的挑衅态度使
中国的抗日运动更加高涨。日本攫取华北的阴谋
绝不会得逞。日军和匪徒入侵绥远的活动因中国
士兵的抵抗而失败。日本对中国的压迫也将以失
败告终。中国人民决心不再对日本做出任何让步，
并准备收复失地，这具有重大意义。
“不幸的是，某些政客对这些局势仍
认识模糊，并因畏惧日本而牺牲了中国利益。这
些政客过分关注日本的实力，而低估了中国人民
的力量。
“以下是日本永远无法战胜中国的原因：
1) 日本的财政实力薄弱；无力维持长期战争。
2) 日本人民反对战争，并对军阀采取的危险政
策感到不满。
3) 日本的军事计划存在缺陷，且战术落后。
4) 中国人民决心抵抗到底。
“日本在远东的地位如此不利，以致
其甚至无法派遣20个师团来与中国作战。即使日
本能派遣20个师团，也不足以取胜，因为分布在全国
各地的训练有素的中国军队已准备为国捐躯。”

February 19, 1937. Afternoon Translation.

Nippo :-

MADAME SUN YAT SEN, GENERAL FENG YU HSIANG AND OTHERS
MAKE JOINT STATEMENT AT THIRD PLENARY SESSION

Madame Sun Yat Sen, General Feng Yu Hsiang
and others who strongly advocate Dr. Sun Yat Sen's Three
Principles of the People and that Soviet Russia, the Chinese
Communist party, Chinese labourers and Chinese peasants
must co-operate as one body in order to save the Chinese
people from becoming slaves, have jointly issued the
following statement to the Third Plenary Session:-
"China is now facing the greatest national
crisis in her history. The eyes of the entire Chinese
people are focussed on the Third Plenary Session which is
now in session at Nanking. China has been driven to the
last stand. A final sacrifice is inevitable. The anti-
Japanese movement has become very strong. The Government
has failed to accept the strong demand. The Chinese people
who can no longer tolerate national humiliation at the
hands of Japan; they will attempt to recover lost territory.
The conclusion of disgraceful treaties with Japan should be
opposed at any cost. It is a matter of regret that we
have a number of politicians who are not able to see the
true situation and who are suffering from an illness called
"fear of Japan". They believe too much about Japan's
strength and under-estimate too much China's strength.
The Japanese people themselves are against war. The
Chinese people are determined to fight to the last soldier.
We are sure that victory will be ours should the Government
put Dr. Sun Yat Sen's will into practice.
"The National Government should immediately
improve the people's livelihood. Some improvements have
been made during the past two or three years in the
construction of railways and communications, but the people's
livelihood has not been improved. Farmers are still suffering
from feudalism and are being forced to pay heavy taxes.
People living in cities are suffering from unemployment.
The only solution is to observe Dr. Sun Yat Sen's will by
improving agriculture and national industries.
"If the Government want to move the people
it should call a general national meeting and select able
men for government service without showing special favour
to members of the Kuomintang. The people should be given
equal suffrage. In order to encourage universal suffrage,
the Government should abolish censorship of publications
as soon as possible and give freedom of speech, assembly
and organization and release all political prisoners.
"It is regrettable that there are
still a number of persons who cannot understand that to
save the country civil war must first be eliminated. It is
ridiculous to say that the communists must first be destroyed
before Japan can be opposed. A militaristic nationalism
is invading our country, therefore our country has been
devastated. We, Chinese, do not want to level our rifles at
our own people. We must first raise a national defence against
a foreign enemy. Our late leader Dr. Sun Yat Sen warned us
not to estrange ourselves from the Powers and to secure
co-operation of Powers such as Soviet Russia, the United
States, Great Britain and France which treat us on an equal
basis."

1937年2月19日。下午译文。

《日日新闻》:-

宋庆龄女士、冯玉祥将军及其他人士在第三届全会上发表联合声明

宋庆龄女士、冯玉祥将军及其他强烈倡导孙中山博士三民主义，并主张苏维埃俄国、中国共产党、中国劳工和中国农民必须团结一致，以使中国人民免于沦为奴隶的人士，向第三届全会联合发表了以下声明:-
“中国正面临其历史上最大的民族危机。全体中国人民的目光都聚焦于正在南京召开的第三届全会。中国已被逼至最后关头。最终的牺牲不可避免。抗日运动已变得非常强劲。政府未能接受这一强烈要求。中国人民再也无法容忍日本造成的民族耻辱；他们将试图收复失地。必须不惜一切代价反对与日本签订屈辱条约。令人遗憾的是，我们有一些政客看不清真实局势，患有一种名为‘恐日病’的病症。他们过分相信日本的实力，而过分低估中国的实力。日本人民本身反对战争。中国人民决心战斗到最后一兵一卒。我们相信，如果政府践行孙中山博士的遗愿，胜利必将属于我们。
“国民政府应立即改善民生。过去两三年在铁路和交通建设方面取得了一些进展，但民生并未得到改善。农民仍受封建主义之苦，被迫缴纳重税。城市居民遭受失业之苦。唯一的解决办法是通过改善农业和民族工业来践行孙中山博士的遗愿。
“如果政府想要动员民众，应召开全国国民会议，选拔能人担任公职，而不特别优待国民党成员。应给予人民平等的选举权。为了鼓励普选，政府应尽快废除出版物审查制度，给予言论、集会和结社自由，并释放所有政治犯。
“令人遗憾的是，仍有许多人无法理解，要拯救国家，必须首先消除内战。说必须先消灭共产党才能抗日，这是荒谬的。军国主义民族主义正在侵入我国，因此我国已遭蹂躏。我们中国人不想将枪口对准自己的同胞。我们必须首先建立针对外敌的国防。我们已故领袖孙中山博士警告我们不要疏远列强，并确保获得如苏维埃俄国、美国、英国和法国等以平等基础对待我们的列强的合作。”

19.2.37
Editorial Comment
The Mainichi publishes the following
leading article:-
The question of China's foreign policy
was discussed by the Third Plenary Session in camera.
General Chang Chun's speech on China's foreign policy,
which was delivered at the Third Plenary Session on
February 17, was not made public. We are suspicious of
such secrecy. Judging from our special telegram from
Nanking, it is clear that China is preparing for war
against Japan and that she does intend to improve Sino-
Japanese relations in a peaceful manner.
The Chinese communist party shocked the
Kuomintang by offering to the Third Plenary Session a
proposal to cancel its plans to overthrow the National
Government and to introduce reforms in Soviet Districts
provided the Kuomintang adopt an anti-Japanese policy.
Mr. Yu Yu Jen, Chairman of the Supervisory Yuan, is reported
to have requested the Session to accept the proposal.
According to certain sources of information, one Chu Yin
Lai, representing the Chinese communist party, called on
General Chiang Kai Shek at Fenghua prior to the submission
of the proposal to the Third Plenary Session and secured
General Chiang Kai Shek's approval for the proposal.
On February 15 an inauguration meeting
of the Various Circles United National Salvation was held.
In the past, the anti-Japanese popular front was opposed
to the national salvation association, but now the two
bodies are working in co-operation.
The Third Plenary Session has restored
the civil rights of General Chang Hsueh Liang, the leader
of the Sian incident, recognized the communist district
in China, halted the anti-communist campaign under the
cloak of unification and ordered the expeditionary forces
to Charhar and East Hopei to suppress the local forces.
pages.zh:
19.2.37
社论评论
《每日新闻》刊登以下社论:-
第三届全会秘密讨论了中国的外交政策问题。张群将军于2月17日在第三届全会上关于中国外交政策的演讲未予公开。我们对这种保密做法表示怀疑。根据我们从南京发出的专电判断，显然中国正在准备对日作战，且并不打算以和平方式改善中日关系。
中国共产党向第三届全会提出一项提议，令国民党感到震惊。该提议称，如果国民党采取抗日政策，中共将取消推翻国民政府的计划，并在苏区实行改革。据报道，监察院院长于右任先生请求全会接受该提议。据某些消息来源称，代表中国共产党的朱寅来（音译）在将该提议提交第三届全会之前，曾在奉化拜访了蒋介石将军，并获得了蒋介石将军对该提议的批准。
2月15日，各界救国联合会举行了成立大会。过去，抗日人民阵线反对救国会，但现在这两个团体正在进行合作。
第三届全会恢复了西安事变领导人张学良将军的公民权利，承认了中国的共产主义地区，停止了打着统一幌子的反共运动，并命令远征军前往察哈尔和冀东镇压地方势力。

pages.en:
Cur. Huc Wan Pao (生活晚报) of February 18 :-
COMMUNIST PARTY'S OFFER TO THE 3RD PLENARY SESSION
Owing to the bandit suppression campaign
launched by the Nanking Government, the Communists in the
North-West are in danger of being wiped out.
According to foreign newspapers, a telegram
in the name of the Communist Party has been sent to the
Third Plenary Session of the Kuomintang. It is learned
that the telegram states (1) that the Communist Party is
willing to give up its armed force, (2) that a reorganization
of the Red Army will be agreed to, (3) that the Party will
surrender to the National Government and (4) that it will
subject itself to the orders of the Military Affairs Commission.
The telegram also contained two strong demands
for freedom of the Press and the release of political
offenders.
pages.zh:
2月18日《生活晚报》:-
共产党向第三届全会提出的提议
由于南京政府发动的剿匪运动，西北地区的共产党人面临被歼灭的危险。
据外国报纸报道，以共产党名义向国民党第三届全会发送了一份电报。据悉，电报内容如下：(1) 共产党愿意放弃其武装力量，(2) 同意重组红军，(3) 该党将归顺国民政府，(4) 并将服从军事委员会的命令。电报还包含两项强烈要求，即新闻自由和释放政治犯。

pages.en:
February 16, 1937. 2. Afternoon Translation.

Hwa Mei Wan Pac dated February 15 :-

CITIZENS FEDERATION'S TELEGRAM TO THIRD PLENARY
SESSION

On the morning of February 15, the Shanghai
First Special District Citizens' Federation and its various
branches sent a telegram containing the following five points
to the Executive and Supervisory members of the Third Plenary
Session:-
(1) It is known to all that the principal
cause of our national crisis is external aggression, lack
of military and political unification and weakness of the
administrative bureau, as witness the recent uprising in
Shensi and Kansu. The Third Plenary Session should devise
ways and means to consolidate the foundation of national
unification.
(2) The political tutelage by the National
Government has lasted ten years. Last year the National
Government proposed the holding of a National Citizens'
Convention to enable the people to participate in the
administration of political affairs. Owing to disturbed
conditions, the proposal could not be carried out. The
Third Plenary Session should fix a date for the convocation
of a National Citizens' Convention so as to strengthen the
foundations of our Government.
(3) The uprising in Shensi and Kansu has
been settled, yet in view of the fact that the trouble
had lasted for more than one month, the remnants of the
bandits were able to revive their activities, thereby causing
great distress to the people of the two provinces. The
Third Plenary Session is, therefore, requested to devise
measures for the relief of the distressed people with a
view to bringing about peace and order in Shensi and Kansu.
(4) The plight of North China is becoming
increasingly dangerous, while the various provinces along
the coast are coveted by the aggressor. For this reason,
we must strengthen our national defence to resist external
invasion. The Third Plenary Session should draw up an
estimate for national defence.
(5) Lastly, the Third Plenary Session
is requested to accelerate economic reconstruction of the
country and improve transportation with a view to improving
the living conditions of the people.

The Holmes (Comment) :-

CHINESE KILLED IN MOTOR CAR ACCIDENT

According to newspaper reports, a Chinese
was killed during the lunar New Year holidays by a motor car
driven by a subject of a friendly nation who was not
qualified to drive a car.
If the driver in this case had been a
Chinese and the victim a subject of the friendly nation,
most probably the residents of Shanghai would have been
busily engaged in removing their homes and would not have
been able to enjoy the New Year holidays.

1937年2月16日。2. 下午译文。

2月15日《华美晚报》:-

市民联合会致第三届全会的电报

2月15日上午，上海第一特区市民联合会及其各分会向第三届全会的执行委员和监察委员发送了一份包含以下五点的电报:-
(1) 众所周知，我国民族危机的主要原因是外部侵略、军事和政治缺乏统一以及行政机构软弱，最近的陕西和甘肃起义即为明证。第三届全会应制定方法和手段以巩固国家统一的基础。
(2) 国民政府的政治训政已持续十年。去年，国民政府提议召开全国国民大会，使人民能够参与政治事务的管理。由于局势动荡，该提议未能实施。第三届全会应确定召开全国国民大会的日期，以加强我国政府的基础。
(3) 陕西和甘肃的起义已平息，但鉴于动乱持续了一个多月，匪徒残余势力得以恢复活动，从而给两省人民造成巨大痛苦。因此，请求第三届全会制定救济受灾人民的措施，以期在陕西和甘肃实现和平与秩序。
(4) 华北的处境日益危险，而沿海各省正被侵略者觊觎。为此，我们必须加强国防以抵抗外部入侵。第三届全会应编制国防预算。
(5) 最后，请求第三届全会加速国家经济重建并改善交通，以期改善人民生活条件。

《字林西报》评论:-

车祸中一名中国人死亡

据报纸报道，农历新年假期期间，一名中国人被一辆由友好国家臣民驾驶的汽车撞死，该驾驶员不具备驾驶资格。
如果本案中的司机是中国人，而受害者是友好国家的臣民，上海居民很可能正忙于搬家，而无法享受新年假期。

February 14, 1937.                                      Morning Translation.

Lih Pao and other local newspapers:

        THE THIRD PLENARY SESSION OF THE KUOMINTANG

        According to information given out by General Yang
Hu, the Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commissioner, General
Chiang Kai Shek will leave for Nanking to-day or to-morrow
to attend the Third Plenary Session of the Kuomintang.

        General Li Tsun Jen, Pacification Commissioner
for Kwangsi, will fly from Hankow to Nanking on the morning
of February 15.

        A telegram from Taiyuan reports that General Yen
Hsi Shan will fly to Nanking to attend the Session.

        General Yu Han Kou, Pacification Commissioner for
Kwangtung, arrived in Shanghai on board the German liner
Gneisenau at 2.30 p.m. yesterday.    He was given a warm
welcome by Mr. T.V. Soong, Mayor Wu Teh Chen, General Yang
Hu, Dr. Wang Chung Hui, and other high government officials.
        At 4 p.m. yesterday, General Yu, accompanied by
Mayor Wu Teh Chen, called on General Chiang Kai Shek to whom
he made a report.
        General Yu will leave for Nanking by the Express
to-night.

1937年2月14日。                                      上午译文。

《立报》及其他本地报纸:

        国民党第三届全会

        据吴淞上海卫戍司令杨虎将军提供的消息，蒋介石将军将于今天或明天前往南京参加国民党第三届全会。

        广西绥靖主任李宗仁将军将于2月15日上午从汉口飞往南京。

        太原来电报告称，阎锡山将军将飞往南京参加会议。

        广东绥靖主任余汉谋将军于昨天下午2时30分乘坐德国邮轮格奈森瑙号抵达上海。他受到了宋子文先生、市长吴铁城、杨虎将军、王宠惠博士及其他政府高官的热情欢迎。
        昨天下午4时，余将军在吴铁城市长的陪同下拜访了蒋介石将军，并向其作了汇报。
        余将军将于今晚乘特快列车前往南京。

Subject Disagreement between members of C.E.C. during session at the
3rd Plenary Conference over policy adopted towards the Red Army.
Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao-liang.

Information has been received from an authentic source
to the effect that during the session of the 3rd Plenary
Conference, hot argument took place between members of C.E.C.
over the question of dealing with the Red Army in the South-
West. A small section of the members supported by Mr. Sun Fo
advocated that peace be made with the leaders of the Red Army,
that the army be given a special area where they can be stationed
and supplied with equipment by the Central Government in order
that their services may be utilized against Japan and so that
China may have a united front to deal with outside aggression.
The proposal was eventually turned down by members of
the Chiang Kai Shek clique assisted by those of the Waung Ching
Wei faction. General Chiang was present when the decision
was made.
Since his return to China, Mr. Waung Ching Wei appears
to have co-operated very harmoniously with General Chiang Kai
Shek and it is largely due to this co-operation that resolutions
put forward by certain opponents advocating a declaration of
war in order to embarrass the Government were not given
consideration.
Rumours have been current that the following changes

Dr. Wong Chung Hui as Minister of Foreign Affairs and
concurrently Vice President of the Executive Yuan.
Mr. Chang Chun to be Mayor of Shanghai.
Mr. Wu Teh Chen as Civil Governor of Kwangtung.
General Chu Shao-liang as Chairman of Anhui Provincial
Government.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. 770
S.2, Special Branch. Section,
REPORT
Date February 23, 1937.
Subject Changes in the Central Tangpu as a result of the 3rd Plenary
Conference.
Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao-liang.

The significant changes that have taken place in
the Central Tangpu as a result of the above conference indicate
that some compromise has been reached between Mr. Waung Ching
Wei and Generalissimo Chiang Kai Shek.
Mr. Chen Kung Po (ex-Minister of Industry and a
strong supporter of the Waung's clique) has been appointed Chief
of the People's Training Department of the Central Tangpu in
place of Mr. Chou Fu Hai ( a member of Chiang's clique). This
important change re-establishes the influence of Mr. Waung's
party in certain sections of the branch Tangpus in China and
will probably prove disadvantageous to the local Tangpu in
connection with its control of labour organizations, especially
in the settlement of labour disputes etc. and will increase
the complications already existing with the Whampoa clique.
I understand that the foreign policy, especially
with regard to Japan, will not be changed. War is not
considered advisable unless the aggression is of such a nature
that it is unbearable. Internally every effort will be made
to effect a strong unification of the country. A decision
was arrived at to continue the campaign against the reds.
There is another important appointment in the
Central Tangpu, that Mr. Tsao Li Tz (ex-Chairman of the Shensi
Provincial Government and at one time Secretary to General
Chiang Kai Shek) to the position of Chief of the People's
Propaganda Department in the place of Mr. Liu Lu Yen, a leader
of the South-West clique (Kwangsi clique).
Other changes in the Government service have not
yet been announced.

U.C. (Special Branch).
Tan Shaoliang
Superintendent.

日期：1937年2月23日。
主题：因第三届全体会议导致的中央党部变动。
由谭绍良警司撰写并呈报。

上述会议导致中央党部发生的重大变化表明，汪精卫先生与蒋介石委员长之间已达成某种妥协。
陈公博先生（前工业部长，汪派系的坚定支持者）已被任命为中央党部民众训练部部长，取代周佛海先生（蒋派系成员）。这一重要变动恢复了汪派在中国各地分部党部某些部门的影响力，这可能对地方党部控制劳工组织（特别是在解决劳资纠纷等方面）产生不利影响，并将加剧与黄埔系之间已存在的复杂关系。

据我了解，外交政策，特别是对日政策，将不会改变。除非侵略性质达到无法忍受的地步，否则认为不宜开战。在内政方面，将竭尽全力实现国家的强力统一。会议决定继续开展“剿共”运动。

中央党部还有另一项重要任命，即曹立之先生（前陕西省政府主席，曾一度担任蒋介石将军的秘书）接替刘芦隐先生（西南派系/桂系领导人）出任中央党部民众宣传部部长。

政府其他人事变动尚未公布。

谭绍良
警司。
